 # frozen_string_literal: true
 
 require "fileutils"
 require "json"
 require "rgeo/geo_json"
 require "map_tiles/configuration"
 
 module MapTiles
   class GeojsonExporter
     attr_reader :configuration, :entity_factory
 
     def initialize(configuration: Configuration.new)
       @configuration = configuration
       @entity_factory = RGeo::GeoJSON::EntityFactory.instance
     end
 
     def export
       FileUtils.mkdir_p(configuration.geojson_dir)
 
       {
         "problems" => write_layer("problems", problem_features),
         "boulders" => write_layer("boulders", boulder_features),
         "areas" => write_layer("areas", area_features),
         "area_hulls" => write_layer("area_hulls", area_hull_features),
         "clusters" => write_layer("clusters", cluster_features),
         "cluster_hulls" => write_layer("cluster_hulls", cluster_hull_features),
         "regions" => write_layer("regions", region_features),
         "region_hulls" => write_layer("region_hulls", region_hull_features),
         "walking_paths" => write_layer("walking_paths", walking_path_features),
         "pois" => write_layer("pois", poi_features)
       }
     end
 
     private
 
     def write_layer(layer_name, features)
       path = configuration.geojson_dir.join("#{layer_name}.geojson")
       collection = entity_factory.feature_collection(features)
       encoded = RGeo::GeoJSON.encode(collection)
       path.write(JSON.pretty_generate(encoded))
       path
     end
 
     def feature(geometry, properties)
       entity_factory.feature(geometry, nil, compact_properties(properties))
     end
 
     def compact_properties(properties)
       properties.each_with_object({}) do |(key, value), result|
         next if value.nil?
         next if value.respond_to?(:empty?) && value.empty?
 
         result[key.to_s] = scalar_value(value)
       end
     end
 
     def scalar_value(value)
       case value
       when BigDecimal
         value.to_f
       else
         value
       end
     end
 
     def problem_features
       Problem.with_location.joins(:area).where(areas: { published: true }).includes(:area).order(:id).filter_map do |problem|
         area = problem.area
         next if problem.location.blank? || area.blank? || area.slug.blank?
 
         name = localized_problem_name(problem, :de)
         name_en = localized_problem_name(problem, :en)
 
         feature(problem.location, {
           problemId: problem.id,
           areaId: area.id,
           areaSlug: area.slug,
           name: name,
-          grade: problem.grade.to_s,
+          grade: problem_grade(problem),
           steepness: problem.steepness,
           featured: problem.featured?,
           boulderId: problem.boulder_id,
           nameEn: different_label(name, name_en),
           popularity: problem.popularity,
           landing: problem.landing,
           height: problem.height,
           parentProblemId: problem.parent_id
         })
       end
     end
 
     def boulder_features
       Boulder.joins(:area).where(areas: { published: true }).where.not(polygon: nil).includes(:area).order(:id).filter_map do |boulder|
         area = boulder.area
         next if area.blank? || area.slug.blank?
 
         feature(boulder.polygon, {
           boulderId: boulder.id,
           areaId: area.id,
           areaSlug: area.slug,
           name: boulder.name
         })
       end
     end
 
     def area_features
       published_areas.filter_map do |area|
         result = hull_result_for_boulders(area.boulders.where(ignore_for_area_hull: false))
         bounds = bounds_for_boulders(area.boulders.where(ignore_for_area_hull: false))
         next if result&.hull.blank? || result&.centroid.blank? || bounds.blank?
 
         feature(result.centroid, area_properties(area, bounds, include_name: true, include_cluster: true))
       end
     end
 
     def area_hull_features
       published_areas.filter_map do |area|
         hull = hull_for_boulders(area.boulders.where(ignore_for_area_hull: false))
         bounds = bounds_for_boulders(area.boulders.where(ignore_for_area_hull: false))
         next if hull.blank? || bounds.blank?
 
         feature(hull, area_properties(area, bounds, include_name: true))
       end
     end
 
     def cluster_features
       published_clusters.filter_map do |cluster|
         area_ids = published_child_areas(cluster).pluck(:id)
         result = hull_result_for_area_ids(area_ids)
         bounds = explicit_or_boulder_bounds(cluster, area_ids)
         point = cluster.center || result&.centroid
         next if point.blank? || bounds.blank?
 
         feature(point, cluster_properties(cluster, bounds, include_name: true))
       end
     end
 
     def cluster_hull_features
       published_clusters.filter_map do |cluster|
         area_ids = published_child_areas(cluster).pluck(:id)
         hull = hull_for_area_ids(area_ids)
         bounds = explicit_or_boulder_bounds(cluster, area_ids)
         next if hull.blank? || bounds.blank?

         south_west_lon: result.south_west_lon.to_f,

    12	    INSTALL_GUIDANCE = <<~TEXT.squish
    13	      Tippecanoe is required to build Austrian Rocks PMTiles. Install it with `brew install tippecanoe` on macOS, or follow https://github.com/mapbox/tippecanoe for your platform, then rerun the build.

    16	    attr_reader :configuration, :executable, :executable_checker, :command_runner
    17	
    18	    def initialize(configuration: Configuration.new, executable: "tippecanoe", executable_checker: nil, command_runner: nil)
    19	      @configuration = configuration
    20	      @executable = executable
    21	      @executable_checker = executable_checker || ->(binary) { executable_on_path?(binary) }
    22	      @command_runner = command_runner || ->(command) { system(*command) }
    23	    end
    24	
    25	    def build(layer_paths:)
    26	      ensure_tippecanoe_available!
    27	      FileUtils.mkdir_p(configuration.output_dir)
    28	
    29	      command = build_command(layer_paths: layer_paths)
    30	      success = command_runner.call(command)
    31	      raise BuildError, "Tippecanoe failed while building #{configuration.artifact_path}" unless success
    32	
    33	      configuration.artifact_path
    34	    end

    36	    def build_command(layer_paths:)
    37	      ordered_layer_paths = LayerContract.layer_names.to_h do |layer_name|
    38	        path = layer_paths.fetch(layer_name) { raise KeyError, "missing GeoJSON path for layer #{layer_name}" }
    39	        [ layer_name, path ]
    40	      end

    44	        "--force",
    45	        "--minimum-zoom=0",
    46	        "--maximum-zoom=#{LayerContract.native_max_zoom}",
    47	        "--output=#{configuration.artifact_path}",
    48	        *ordered_layer_paths.flat_map { |layer_name, path| [ "--named-layer=#{layer_name}:#{path}" ] }
    49	      ]
    50	    end
    51	
    52	    private

    55	      return if executable_checker.call(executable)

1	# Austrian Rocks PMTiles Overlay Contract
     2	
     3	This is the consumer and maintainer contract for the Austrian Rocks PMTiles overlay artifact. It intentionally lives in `/docs/`, and `/docs/` remains gitignored for now, so this file is a local untracked/ignored working artifact rather than a committed repository file.
     4	
     5	## Artifact and delivery rules
     6	
     7	- Artifact basename: `austrian-rocks`.
     8	- File type: PMTiles built with Tippecanoe from deterministic per-layer GeoJSON exports.
     9	- native max zoom: `16` for every source layer. MapLibre, web, and iOS clients may overzoom above `16`.
    10	- Generated files are build artifacts only and must stay under ignored output such as `tmp/map_tiles/`; production must not depend on Rails serving `public/maps/austrian-rocks.pmtiles`.
    11	- Bunny/CDN publication writes both:
    12	  - Immutable version: `<prefix>/austrian-rocks-<version>.pmtiles`
    13	  - Stable latest: `<prefix>/austrian-rocks-latest.pmtiles`
    14	- Public URLs are built from map-specific CDN configuration plus the object key, for example `https://<MAP_TILES_PUBLIC_CDN_HOST>/<prefix>/austrian-rocks-<version>.pmtiles`.
    15	- Bunny storage credentials may reuse the existing Bunny S3-compatible environment variables, but map tile CDN host, object prefix, and version are map-specific configuration.
    16	
    17	## Naming and data rules
    18	
    19	- Source layer names are snake_case and stable.
    20	- Feature properties are camelCase, scalar vector-tile values. If relationship metadata needs structure, encode it as a documented JSON string.
    21	- Feature IDs are stable scalar model identifiers exposed as explicit properties such as `problemId`, `areaId`, or `walkingPathId`.
    22	- Consumers must build app navigation from IDs and slugs. PMTiles features must not contain app-local canonical URL properties.
    23	- Localized labels use required `name` plus optional `nameEn` only when an English value exists and differs from `name`. If a model has no English source field, omit `nameEn`.
    24	- POIs may include external `googleUrl`; this is not an app-local canonical URL.
    25	- Circuit layers and circuit properties are intentionally excluded and must not be introduced.
    26	- `problems.boulderId` is optional and comes from the database relationship cleanup delivered by completed item `0007`.
    27	- `walking_paths` reads line geometry from `WalkingPath` records where `published` is true, using the source delivered by completed item `0007`; `0004` must not add or recreate walking-path schema/admin foundations.
    28	
    29	## PMTiles source layers vs MapLibre style layers
    30	
    31	The layers below are PMTiles source layers. Later MapLibre styles can derive many visual style layers from the same source layer:
    32	
    33	- Region, cluster, area, and boulder text labels can render from `regions`, `clusters`, `areas`, and `boulders`.
    34	- Polygon fills and outline line styles can render from `region_hulls`, `cluster_hulls`, `area_hulls`, and `boulders`.
    35	- `walking_paths` renders as one or more line style layers.
    36	- Problem symbols, boulder labels, POI symbols, and POI labels can be separate style layers without changing this source contract.
    37	
    38	## Source layer contract
    39	
    40	### `problems`
    41	
    42	- Geometry: `Point`
    43	- Stable identifier: `problemId`
    44	- Required properties: `problemId`, `areaId`, `areaSlug`, `name`, `grade`, `steepness`, `featured`
    45	- Optional properties: `boulderId`, `nameEn`, `popularity`, `landing`, `height`, `parentProblemId`
    46	- Source notes: export only problems with locations in published areas. `grade` is always present; blank Rails grades are exported as the scalar string `unknown`. `boulderId` is present only when the `0007` relationship assignment knows the containing boulder.
    47	- Navigation: open a problem by `problemId`, optionally scoped by `areaSlug`.
    48	
    49	### `boulders`
    50	
    51	- Geometry: `Polygon`
    52	- Stable identifier: `boulderId`
    53	- Required properties: `boulderId`, `areaId`, `areaSlug`
    54	- Optional properties: `name`
    55	- Source notes: export boulder polygons from published areas. `ignore_for_area_hull` affects hull derivation only; it does not exclude the boulder polygon from this layer.
    56	- Navigation: select the boulder by `boulderId` and use `areaSlug` for area context.
    57	
    58	### `areas`
    59	
    60	- Geometry: `Point`
    61	- Stable identifier: `areaId`
    62	- Required properties: `areaId`, `areaSlug`, `name`, `priority`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
    63	- Optional properties: `nameEn`, `shortName`, `clusterId`, `clusterSlug`
    64	- Source notes: point geometry is the label/selection point for a published area; bounds describe the area extent.
    65	- Navigation: open an area by `areaSlug` or `areaId`.
    66	
    67	### `area_hulls`
    68	
    69	- Geometry: `Polygon`
    70	- Stable identifier: `areaId`
    71	- Required properties: `areaId`, `areaSlug`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
    72	- Optional properties: `name`, `nameEn`, `priority`
    73	- Source notes: hull geometries are derived from non-ignored boulders in published areas.
    74	- Navigation: treat taps as area selections by `areaSlug` or `areaId`.
    75	
    76	### `clusters`
    77	
    78	- Geometry: `Point`
    79	- Stable identifier: `clusterId`
    80	- Required properties: `clusterId`, `clusterSlug`, `name`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
    81	- Optional properties: `nameEn`, `regionId`, `regionSlug`, `mainAreaId`, `mainAreaSlug`
    82	- Source notes: point geometry is the label/selection point for a published cluster.
    83	- Navigation: open a cluster by `clusterSlug` or `clusterId`.
    84	
    85	### `cluster_hulls`
    86	
    87	- Geometry: `Polygon`
    88	- Stable identifier: `clusterId`
    89	- Required properties: `clusterId`, `clusterSlug`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
    90	- Optional properties: `name`, `nameEn`, `regionId`, `regionSlug`, `mainAreaId`, `mainAreaSlug`
    91	- Source notes: hull geometries are derived from non-ignored boulders in published child areas.
    92	- Navigation: treat taps as cluster selections by `clusterSlug` or `clusterId`.
    93	
    94	### `regions`
    95	
    96	- Geometry: `Point`
    97	- Stable identifier: `regionId`
    98	- Required properties: `regionId`, `regionSlug`, `name`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
    99	- Optional properties: `nameEn`, `mainClusterId`, `mainClusterSlug`
   100	- Source notes: point geometry is the label/selection point for a published region.
   101	- Navigation: open a region by `regionSlug` or `regionId`.
   102	
   103	### `region_hulls`
   104	
   105	- Geometry: `Polygon`
   106	- Stable identifier: `regionId`
   107	- Required properties: `regionId`, `regionSlug`, `southWestLat`, `southWestLon`, `northEastLat`, `northEastLon`
   108	- Optional properties: `name`, `nameEn`, `mainClusterId`, `mainClusterSlug`
   109	- Source notes: hull geometries are derived from non-ignored boulders in published descendant clusters/areas.
   110	- Navigation: treat taps as region selections by `regionSlug` or `regionId`.
   111	
   112	### `walking_paths`
   113	
   114	- Geometry: `LineString` or `MultiLineString`
   115	- Stable identifier: `walkingPathId`
   116	- Required properties: `walkingPathId`, `slug`, `name`
   117	- Optional properties: `nameEn`, `description`
   118	- Source notes: export only `WalkingPath` records where `published` is true and valid SRID 4326 line geometry is present. `name` comes from the walking-path label/name source; omit `nameEn` unless an English source value exists later.
   119	- Navigation: use `walkingPathId` or `slug` for path selection. Walking paths are general approach/connector overlays and are not POI route geometries.
   120	
   121	### `pois`
   122	
   123	- Geometry: `Point`
   124	- Stable identifier: `poiId`
   125	- Required properties: `poiId`, `poiType`, `name`, `accessAreasJson`
   126	- Optional properties: `shortName`, `googleUrl`
   127	- Source notes: export POIs with locations and public consumer-safe metadata. `googleUrl` is an external URL and is allowed.
   128	- Navigation: select a POI by `poiId`; use `accessAreasJson` to present related area access metadata.
   129	
   130	`accessAreasJson` is a JSON string, not an object-valued vector-tile property. It is derived from `poi_routes` and contains an array of entries with these scalar keys:
   131	
   132	```json
   133	[
   134	  {
   135	    "areaId": 123,
   136	    "areaSlug": "zillertal",
   137	    "transport": "walking",
   138	    "distance": 1200,
   139	    "minutes": 15
   140	  }
   141	]
   142	```
   143	
   144	The value documents access metadata only. It must not be interpreted as route geometry and must not replace `walking_paths`.
   145	
   146	## Expected layer list
   147

# Pmtiles Overlay Contract — review

### Strengths
- docs/map_tiles.md:9 and docs/map_tiles.md:40-docs/map_tiles.md:159 — the ignored consumer contract still documents native max zoom `16` and all ten required PMTiles source layers with geometry, identifiers, properties, and navigation guidance.
- lib/map_tiles/layer_contract.rb:11-lib/map_tiles/layer_contract.rb:72 and lib/map_tiles/layer_contract.rb:92 — `LayerContract` centralizes the ten source layers, native max zoom, camelCase properties, and a circuit-field guard, giving exporter/tests a single contract source.
- lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:66-lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:89 and lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:337-lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:347 — the P2 rework now preserves required problem `grade` with an explicit `unknown` fallback and keeps required labels present through source-field/fallback display labels.
- lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:172-lib/map_tiles/geojson_exporter.rb:190 — published walking paths and POI `accessAreasJson` are exported in the planned scalar shape without app-local canonical URL properties.
